The online option is ideal for working professionals while being on campus provides greater opportunities for interdisciplinary coursework and research collaboration. On-campus students are also eligible to be considered for graduate assistantship positions. Ph.D. students in aviation at SLU a qualifying exam that focuses on topics related to the coursework and assesses general preparation for graduate research. [2, 3] These elements will collectively prepare students for successful careers and address the evolving needs of the region, nation and world. [2, 3] As part of their degrees, the students will take graduate-level courses to deepen their knowledge, understanding, and skills in the discipline as well as perform independent discovery or design-focused original research under the guidance of SLU's graduate faculty members. Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Medicine Technology (NMT) at Saint Louis University prepares graduates for entry-level positions as nuclear medicine technologists. [2] Nuclear medicine is a medical specialty that uses safe, painless, and cost-effective techniques to image the body and treat disease. [2] It utilizes small amounts of radioactive materials to diagnose and treat diseases with gamma cameras or PET/CT scanners, uniquely documenting organ function and structure. [2] This method can provide information that might otherwise require surgery or more expensive diagnostic tests. [4] The program's curriculum includes all basic sciences and an intensive NMT curriculum with 1,000 hours of clinical practicum. [4] Upon completion, graduates are eligible for national certification to become a certified nuclear medicine technologist (CNMT). [4]
Accredidation: The program was first accredited in 1971 by the Joint Review Committee on Educational Programs in Nuclear Medicine Technology (JRCNMT), in collaboration with the American College of Radiology, the American Society of Radiologic Technologists, the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging, and the Technologist Section of the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging. [10] This accreditation has been continuous. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics
Description: The field of nutrition and dietetics celebrates the central role of food in shaping health and enhancing well-being. This interdisciplinary field blends nutrition science with practical applications to promote healthy lifestyles, prevent disease, and enhance quality of life. [2, 8] Saint Louis University students in this program delve into the nuances of nutritional assessment, meal planning, and the broader influence of food on physical and mental health. [2, 8] The program provides a strong foundation for pre-health pathways, emphasizing a unique "food as medicine" approach, where students explore how nutrition is a powerful tool in preventing and managing chronic diseases. [2] Students can gain hands-on experience at the Fresh Gatherings Café and Farm, a student-run dining facility, to plan, prepare, and serve meals made from locally sourced ingredients. [2, 8] The curriculum is noted for its food-first philosophy, with a strong foundation in culinary arts and sustainable foods. [8] Graduates are prepared for careers in healthcare, the culinary world, or public health, with the option to become registered dietitian nutritionists (RDNs). [2, 8]
Accredidation: The didactic program in dietetics is accredited by The Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND). [10] Graduates who successfully complete the ACEND-accredited program at Saint Louis University are eligible to apply to an ACEND-accredited supervised practice program and apply to take the CDR credentialing exam to become a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN). [8]

The discipline of political sciencecoversmanytopics,fromcampaignsand elections in the United Statesto an economic development and democratization worldwideto diplomacy and globalization. Political science majors learn to address big questions, such as what makes a government legitimate or what constitutes a good society. They also come to understand causes and mechanisms for addressing significant global challenges like terrorism, poverty, climate change and war. Political science students at Saint Louis University pursue jobs in government, international organizations, nonprofit organizations, education, law, journalism, diplomacy, survey research and fields related to promoting social justice.

A political science minor is a valuable addition for any major, as law and politics will inevitably impact your chosen career. For students in fields like criminal justice, a political science minor provides a better understanding of how law and politics affect the criminal justice system. If you are majoring in secondary education with plans to teach history, civics, government, or social science, a political science minor is beneficial. History majors will find that a political science minor helps in understanding the political context of historical events. For business or economics majors, this minor is important due to the deep connection between the political, business, and economic spheres. Sociology majors will gain an understanding of how to influence public policies related to social support services. Journalism majors who intend to cover politics will benefit from the minor by understanding the political framework, processes, and terminology. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Radiation Therapy
Description: If you major in radiation therapy at Saint Louis University, you will learn to treat cancer patients with high-energy radiation using highly specialized equipment. You will focus on helping plan and administer prescribed doses of radiation to affected areas as directed by a radiation oncologist. A radiation therapist is a health care professional skilled in the art and science of medical radiation treatment. Therapists are primarily concerned with the design and administration of radiation therapy treatment, in addition to issues of daily well-being for patients with cancer. A therapist is responsible for administering the prescribed treatment dose of radiation using high-energy linear accelerators. These treatments are provided to cure the patient or control the disease, improving patients' quality of life. Therapists also monitor patients' reactions for radiation side effects and keep highly accurate records of planning, treatment and equipment use. This profession combines the great satisfaction of helping others during difficult times with sophisticated technological equipment and scientific techniques. Radiation therapists work as part of a multidisciplinary health care team with radiation oncologists, medical physicists, dosimetrists, nurses and other medical specialists to provide the best treatment and support available to their patients.
Accredidation: The Radiation Therapy Program at Saint Louis University is fully accredited by the Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology (JRCERT), having been awarded an eight-year accreditation. [22] It is the only JRCERT-accredited radiation therapy program in the state of Missouri. [22] The program's next scheduled reaccreditation review by the JRCERT will be July 2025. [22] The program's current award is eight years. [22]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social Work
Description: A bachelor's degree in social work from Saint Louis University gives students the skills to improve the quality of life for individuals or communities facing difficulties such as poverty, serious illness or disability. Social workers seek to help individuals, families, groups and communities address life challenges. SLU's Bachelor of Science in Social Work prepares students for generalist social work practice integrating knowledge and skills with field experience. [17] The social work curriculum contains 42 credits of major courses covering topics such as human behavior and the social environment and four practice courses that address social work with individuals, families, groups, organizations and communities. [17] During senior year, students spend two semesters in a social service agency, supervised by an experienced social worker. [17]
Accredidation: The social work bachelor's program is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). [9] Saint Louis University's Bachelor of Science in Social Work (B.S.S.W.) has been fully accredited since 1974. [15] The program was last accredited in 2018, and the next accreditation is scheduled for 2026. [15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Social Work

Description: Saint Louis University offers an undergraduate minor in social work that can be completed in 18 credits. A minor in social work provides SLU students with an understanding of the social work profession, the issues that social work addresses and the values that drive the profession. [7] Students considering pursuing an M.S.W. will not be able to obtain advanced standing toward the M.S.W. with a minor in social work. [7] Only students with a Bachelor of Science in Social Work (https://catalog.slu.edu/colleges-schools/social-work/social-work-bs/) can obtain advanced standing. [7]
Accredidation: The social work bachelor's and master's programs are accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). [4] The catalog for the Minor in Social Work does not explicitly state its own accreditation status, but it notes that only students with a Bachelor of Science in Social Work can obtain advanced standing for a Master of Social Work (M.S.W.). [7]

Description: Students who major in sociology at Saint Louis University engage in the scientific study of human groups and their characteristics, changes, causes and consequences. [2, 3] Through teaching, research and service, sociology reveals a critical understanding of the different ways people relate to one another through the organization of society and how its structures and cultures influence lives. [2, 3] At Saint Louis University, the Bachelor of Arts in Sociology program's subject matter ranges from family life to large-scale organizations, from crime to religion, from the divisions of race and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture, from poverty to prosperity and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sport. [2, 3] Few fields have such a broad and exciting scope. [2, 3] SLU's bachelor's degree in sociology curricula include exciting fieldwork practicum courses and service-learning. [2, 3]

Through teaching, research and service, faculty and students in Saint Louis University's sociology program reveal a critical understanding of the ways people relate to one another through the organization of society and how its structures and cultures influence our lives. [3, 8] Subject matter in sociology courses at SLU ranges from family life to large-scale organizations, from crime to religion, from the divisions of race and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture, from poverty to prosperity, from the sociology of work to the sociology of sport. [3, 8] Students must complete a minimum total of 21 credits for the minor — nine credits of required coursework and 12 credits of electives. [3, 8]

The Bachelor of Arts in Spanish at Saint Louis University prepares students for careers that require Spanish proficiency or for graduate studies in Spanish. [3] The program aims for students to achieve oral and written proficiency in Spanish through courses in literature, culture, linguistics, and Spanish for professional contexts. [3] The curriculum, which requires 120 credits in total with 33 credits from Spanish coursework, provides a deep understanding of Hispanic societies through literary, cultural, and linguistic analyses. [3] Students are required to complete 18 credits of literature or advanced Spanish language study. [2] There is also an option to study at the SLU-Madrid campus, which has a focus on advanced language training, as well as cultural and literary studies. [2]
Accredidation: Saint Louis University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [13] The next comprehensive evaluation is scheduled for 2031-32. [13]

Description: Saint Louis University offers an undergraduate minor in Spanish on its main campus and at SLU-Madrid. Speaking a language other than English is necessary in an increasingly globalized, complex world. A minor in Spanish can complement nearly any major, especially those related to education, health sciences, law, international studies, political science, psychology, social work, sociology, biology or humanities, and can be completed at SLU with just 18 credits. With the help of a team of dedicated, experienced instructors and mentors, Spanish minors at SLU build connections with Hispanic cultures by refining their language skills in Spanish, developing interculturalVIA competence, exploring the Hispanic cultural legacy and gaining familiarity with Spanish within professional contexts. Throughout their coursework, Spanish minors develop critical, analytical and language skills.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
Description: The field of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences (SLHS) is comprised of two distinct professions: speech-language pathology and audiology. These professions are concerned with human communication and its disorders. A desire for a career in service is a primary motivation for students who study SLHS. Speech-language pathologists help prevent, identify, assess, and provide treatment for communication and swallowing disorders - to improve outcomes and quality of life for the client and their families. This includes language development, acquired language disorders, stuttering, and voice and articulation disorders.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sport Business
Department: Richard A. Chaifetz School of Business
Description: The sports industry generates hundreds of billions of dollars each year. Major sports teams, universities and recreational leagues employ people educated in sports business to conduct daily business operations. At Saint Louis University's Richard A. Chaifetz School of Business, students may pursue a Bachelor of Science in Sports Business or include a minor in sports business in addition to their chosen major. Housed in the Chaifetz School of Business's Department of Management, SLU's sports business major is interdisciplinary and includes courses in management, marketing and economics. This mix of courses gives sports business students the skills needed for careers in college and amateur athletics, facility and event management, professional teams and leagues, sports merchandising, leisure and fitness, and sports media.
Accredidation: The Richard A. Chaifetz School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) at the bachelor's and master's levels.

Department: Richard A. Chaifetz School of Business
Description: The SLU interdisciplinary sports business minor offers students the option to take courses in three different disciplines. Students gain practical knowledge through a capstone project and have the opportunity to supplement classwork through internships and participation in the Sports Business Association, a Richard A. Chaifetz School of Business student organization.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Strategic and Organizational Communication
Description: The ability to communicate effectively and ethically is essential for success in personal and professional life. The Bachelor of Arts in Communication at Saint Louis University provides students with a comprehensive understanding of communication theories, research, and practices. The program is designed to develop students’ critical thinking, message analysis, and communication skills across various contexts. Students in the B.A. in Communication program choose from three concentrations: 'Journalism,' 'Media Studies,' and 'Strategic and Organizational Communication.' Each concentration offers a focused curriculum that prepares students for specific career paths within the broader field of communication.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Studio Art

Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Theatre is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Arts in Theatre is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST). [1]

Description: The Minor in Theatre offers students a comprehensive overview of the study of theatre, including both academic (history and criticism) and production (acting, design and technology) courses. The purpose is to expose undergraduate students to the field by reinforcing the integrated nature of theatre as a scholarly and aesthetic pursuit. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theological Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in theological studies at Saint Louis University allows you to study and value the most important aspects of religious experience and thought. It is rooted in the Catholic tradition but seen in the context of the whole Christian tradition and in dialogue with the other world's religious traditions. [18] The program allows students to explore major questions about life and God while studying with top scholars in the field. [18] Students develop writing, research and critical thinking skills in preparation for graduate study and careers in various disciplines such as theology, law, social work, philosophy and many others. [18]

The minor in theological studies, offered by the Department of Theological Studies, provides a foundation in the study of religion across the globe, with a particular focus on Catholic and other Christian traditions. Courses offered by the department traverse a range of research methods, religious traditions, historical periods and places around the world. The minor allows flexibility for students to pursue nine credit hours of their choice, providing broadly applicable training in religion and faith, along with skills in research, critical thinking and communication that are helpful for any career.

Description: Saint Louis University's minor in women's and gender studies can be relatively easy to combine with another major or additional minor. [6] Women's and gender studies elective courses are often cross-listed with other departments, enabling students to use one course to simultaneously fulfill requirements for both their women's and gender studies minor and their other major and minors. [6] To complete the minor, students take the introductory course options, take two courses from two of the four other distribution areas required for the major (Diversity and Identity; Praxis; Theory; Inquiry/Research Experience), and take three electives at the 2000-level or above from courses with either a WGST number, a WGST cross-listing or a WGST attribute. [6, 8] The minor requires a total of 18 credits. [6, 8] Courses may simultaneously count for multiple majors and minors, and for core requirements. [6, 8] No single course can count for both a required course and an elective for a women's and gender studies major/minor. [6, 8]
